facts.fact: Hari is the Shepherd's Stair route-keeper, who has kept the stair thirty winters as his father did; his hut at the Stair's foot has been burned and his fate is unknown.
facts.why: needed because the beat names Hari's burned hut and Kunal's fear for him.

facts.fact: The Shepherd's Stair's lower ice steps number forty-one by Ila's count, including a hand-high half-step under the first overhang that Kunal's family does not count.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Ila correct his count to forty-one.

facts.fact: A route-keeper's marker stone at the head of the Stair carries fresh chalk in old hill script: 'They ask for the princes' way.' with a second line begun and smeared out.
facts.why: needed because the beat's closing image requires the warning stone.
